issues.description: Runtime dependency pin on setuptools<82 conflates a CI workaround with a product constraint.
issues.detail: The two shell scripts pin setuptools<82 for build/install — that is the actual workaround. Adding setuptools<82 to core/setup.py install_requires complects a transient upstream bug (mmcv issue 3325) with every downstream consumer's runtime environment, and outlives the CI fix. Pin the cap in CI only, or scope it to the mmcv extra.

issues.description: FIXME comment lives in two places but the third (core/setup.py) has no link back to the upstream issue.
issues.detail: The two shell FIXMEs cite mmcv#3325; the setup.py pin does not. When mmcv fixes the bug, the shell pins will be found and reverted, and the setup.py pin will silently linger. Either drop the runtime pin or annotate it with the same FIXME and revert criterion so the time-bound nature of the constraint is explicit.

issues.description: mmdet version bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 without a stated reason in the diff.
issues.detail: The PR is framed as 'fix mmengine failure,' but mmdet also moved a minor version. That is a separate fact about the world from the setuptools workaround and deserves its own line of justification — otherwise a future reader cannot tell which change fixed what, and rollback becomes guesswork.

issues.description: Switch from mim to pip with --no-build-isolation is a meaningful semantic change that is undocumented.
issues.detail: mim resolves the openmim ecosystem; pip --no-build-isolation reuses the ambient setuptools<82 to satisfy mmcv's build. That is the actual mechanism by which the workaround functions. A one-line comment explaining why --no-build-isolation is required would let the next maintainer reason about removing it when the upstream is fixed.

review.summary: The CI-side fix is reasonable and well-scoped — pin setuptools<82 in build_pkg and in setup_mmcv.sh to dodge a known upstream regression in mmcv. The concerning move is bleeding that workaround into core/setup.py's install_requires, which complects a transient CI build constraint with every downstream user's runtime environment and lacks the FIXME breadcrumb the shell scripts carry. The mmdet bump and the mim-to-pip switch are real semantic changes that deserve their own one-line justifications so future maintainers can decompose 'what fixed mmengine' from 'what else moved.' Decision: COMPLECTED on the setup.py pin; the rest is INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY honestly labeled.
